parts.note: bridge is a partnership card game

explanation.surface: An instruction to cut short a hand of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to condense or cut it down, a direct synonym of shorten.

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
E is a musical note
D is another musical note

explanation.surface: Silverware brought out ahead of the banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used before' just places the silver ahead of the two notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Aged means advanced in years, a plain synonym of old.

definitions.meaning: a crop plant grown for oilseed

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a grave offence and the yellow-flowered oilseed crop cultivated in fields.

definitions.meaning: to dragoon someone is to force or coerce them

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a plural noun for mounted troops and a verb form meaning coerces.

clue.text: Looking at money in government stocks

indicators.note: stocks in the sense of holds or keeps a supply of, so these words contain the answer

explanation.surface: An investor considering putting cash into gilts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocks' looks like part of the financial picture but it is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeing something means looking at it closely, here in its shorter spelling.

indicators.note: breaking suggests the two words are smashed apart and their letters reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone forever flouting the law, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' shuffles the six letters of LAW and SAY together.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something always means doing it constantly, without a break, a straight synonym.

clue.text: They take silk before becoming high fliers

definitions.text: They take silk before becoming high fliers

parts.words: They take silk before becoming high fliers
parts.note: reads like barristers becoming QCs before rising in their career, but describes young insects spinning cocoons before turning into moths

explanation.walkthrough: To take silk is to become a senior barrister in Britain; here it means spinning silk.
explanation.definitionFit: Caterpillars and silkworms are immature insects that spin silk before emerging as winged adults.

indicators.note: breaks means the word strain is broken up and its letters reordered

parts.note: a gent is a man, a gentleman

explanation.surface: A man cracking under severe pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' turns STRAIN into ASTRIN, which is followed by GENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Astringent criticism is harsh or severe, a figurative sense of the word.

parts.note: sounds like a promotion prospect for sailors, but refers to the highest tidal rise predicted for those at sea

explanation.definitionFit: The tide with the greatest rise and fall, occurring at new and full moon, is what sailors would be warned of.

indicators.note: split tells us the letters of these two words come apart and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Trousers whose hip seams burst under strain.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphasis is the stress placed on a word or idea, a synonym in that sense.

parts.note: reads like someone living at a smart address, but address here means a formal speech

explanation.definitionFit: A public speaker who delivers addresses well is a skilled speechmaker, the sense here.

clue.text: Importance of the wig in disguise

indicators.note: disguise suggests the letters are altered into a different form

explanation.surface: A wig worn as a disguise, given great significance.
explanation.definitionFit: Weight in the sense of influence or significance, as in an argument carrying weight.

clue.text: People in the services go on creating mayhem

indicators.note: mayhem is chaos, so the letters of the preceding words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Churchgoers who carry on causing havoc during worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mayhem' rearranges the twelve letters of GO ON CREATING.
explanation.definitionFit: A congregation is the body of worshippers attending church services.

clue.text: Produces a large stake and wins a fortune

definitions.meaning: a pile is a large post driven into the ground, so this reads literally as producing one
to make a pile is to earn a great deal of money

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for getting rich doubles as a literal description of making a heavy wooden post.

clue.text: Be clearly out when turning ball goes to fielder

parts.note: break is the turn of a cricket ball off the pitch
cover is a fielding position in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricketer dismissed when a spinning delivery is caught by a fielder.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a cricket dismissal; COVER is a fielding position on the off side. 'goes to' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave a hiding place and come into the open is to emerge clearly into view.

parts.note: HMS Pinafore is a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta, but a pinafore is also a garment worn over clothes, suggesting a theatre area named after such a garment

explanation.walkthrough: A pinafore is a kind of apron; an apron stage is the part of a stage projecting in front of the curtain.
explanation.definitionFit: The forestage jutting out beyond the proscenium arch is so called, matching the garment pun.

parts.note: a high boy's voice, and a word also meaning threefold, so a member of a group of three

explanation.definitionFit: A boy soprano is so called, and the word also means triple or three times as much.

indicators.note: back signals that the word for haul is written in reverse

parts.note: to haul is to tug or pull

explanation.surface: An angler reeling in the line.
explanation.definitionFit: Gut, catgut made from animal intestine, was traditionally used for fishing line.

clue.text: Without transport, without direction, but unconcerned

parts.note: a car is a means of transport
E is east, a compass direction
less means without

explanation.surface: Someone with no car and no sense of direction who does not mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Being careless means not bothering or worrying, so unconcerned is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Maybe many decades are viewed in retrospect

indicators.note: looking back suggests the little word is read from right to left

explanation.surface: Decades that seem long only when looked back on.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a long historical period, which may well span many decades.

indicators.note: inside places the filtering word within the pipe

parts.note: a reed is a simple pipe or the vibrating part of a woodwind instrument
to strain liquid is to filter it

explanation.surface: Someone having inspected the filter within a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Restrained means held back or kept in check, so it can stand for checked.

clue.text: Girl to see a chap on half days

parts.note: a chap is a man
a chap is a man

indicators.note: half takes the first two of the four letters of days

explanation.surface: A girl arranging to see a man on alternate half days.
explanation.definitionFit: Amanda is a girl's given name.

definitions.meaning: a task ... has been achieved or carried out
an ... player is skilled or expert

explanation.definitionFit: The word works both as a past participle meaning achieved and as an adjective meaning highly skilled.

clue.text: Heavenly body, one seen in flight

indicators.note: seen in places the numeral within the heavenly body

parts.note: a star is a heavenly body
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A shooting star or other object spotted in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' looks like flying through the sky, but it means a set of steps; STAIR can mean a whole staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair can mean a flight of steps, as in a winding stair.

definitions.meaning: to ... a mark or name is to display it

explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both carrying visibly, as a coat of arms, and putting up with something.

clue.text: Left in charge but run away

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the charge

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service

explanation.surface: Someone left in charge who nonetheless runs off.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee is to run away from danger, a direct synonym.

clue.text: In a hole? Use your ingenuity

parts.note: a vent is an opening or hole

explanation.surface: Stuck in a tight spot, you are told to think your way out.
explanation.definitionFit: To devise something new requires ingenuity, so inventing is using it.

parts.note: fare is food provided, as in good plain fare
a well is a source of water

explanation.surface: Someone abandoning their food and drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm off' is what someone says when leaving, so the definition is a parting word.
explanation.definitionFit: A goodbye said on departure is exactly what someone leaving announces with these words.

clue.text: Organ swell may affect one's hearing

parts.note: the ear is the organ of hearing
to wax is to grow or swell, as the moon does

explanation.surface: A swelling organ, perhaps an inflamed one, could dull your hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A build-up of cerumen in the canal can muffle sound and impair hearing.

definitions.meaning: a stock held back for later use

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb meaning to book in advance and a noun meaning a stockpile kept back.
